title: Physical models
scope: Infinite translation-invariant finite-range qubit lattice interactions, with a finite number of qubits per cell.
interaction_convention: H = sum_cell translate(h0); terms are h0; e=<h0>/qubits_per_cell

conventions.site: A site is (cell, qubit): cell is an integer d-tuple and qubit is a zero-based index within the unit cell.
conventions.pauli: Each term is a coefficient times a finite Hermitian Pauli word. X, Y and Z denote Pauli matrices, not spin matrices.
conventions.spin: Conventional spin-1/2 exchange uses S=sigma/2. The frozen Pauli coefficients already include all required factors, including the 1/4 in Heisenberg exchange terms.
conventions.translation: One listed local interaction density h0 is translated over every unit cell. Cell translations do not permute qubit species.
conventions.energy: The energy density per physical qubit is omega(h0)/q, where q is qubits_per_cell.
conventions.infinite_sum: H denotes a local interaction family, not a bounded infinite operator sum.
conventions.constants: Identity terms, including projector offsets, are retained exactly.

families.name: Ising & plaquette
families.description: Local Ising interactions, transverse fields and multispin plaquettes test quantum fluctuations across one, two and three dimensions.

families.name: Exchange & frustration
families.description: Spin exchange on chains, ladders and frustrated lattices spans anisotropy, dimerization, chirality and quantum spin ice.

families.name: Compass & Kitaev
families.description: Bond direction selects the spin component, from compass interactions to honeycomb and three-dimensional tricoordinated Kitaev lattices.

families.name: Cluster & SPT
families.description: Multiqubit cluster and symmetry-protected topological fixed-point Hamiltonians provide structured entangled-state targets.

families.name: Topological codes
families.description: Local commuting operators on faces, stars and cells define topologically ordered spin and quantum-code Hamiltonians.

families.name: Fracton codes
families.description: Three-dimensional commuting Pauli models exhibit restricted excitation motion and geometry beyond ordinary topological codes.

notes: This is the complete physical-model library. The displayed historical leaderboard evaluated only the ten task IDs identified separately.
Descriptions and family labels are editorial summaries of the frozen interactions. The exact mathematical task definitions are the original terms, parameters and cell conventions below.
Frozen solvability codes are retained for provenance only and are not a universal claim that a global exact ground-state energy has been established.
The qubit-only fifty-task catalogue does not include a Fermi-Hubbard task.

models.name: Transverse-field Ising chain
models.description: Ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor ZZ interactions compete with a transverse X field on an infinite chain.

models.name: Mixed-field Ising chain
models.description: A longitudinal Z field adds a second field direction to the nearest-neighbor transverse-field Ising chain.

models.name: ANNNI chain
models.description: Competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor Ising interactions are combined with a transverse field.

models.name: Anisotropic XY chain
models.description: Unequal XX and YY nearest-neighbor couplings interact with a transverse Z field.

models.name: Longitudinal-field XXZ chain
models.description: Anisotropic nearest-neighbor exchange competes with a longitudinal field on an infinite chain.

models.name: Zero-field XYZ chain
models.description: Three unequal nearest-neighbor spin-component couplings define an anisotropic chain without an external field.

models.name: J1-J2 Heisenberg chain (Majumdar-Ghosh point)
models.description: Nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor spin-1/2 exchange is fixed at a known dimer ground-state point.

models.name: Cluster chain
models.description: Commuting ZXZ operators couple each chain qubit to its two neighbors.

models.name: Cluster-Ising chain
models.description: Three-site XZX cluster interactions compete with nearest-neighbor YY interactions.

models.name: Alternating compass chain
models.description: XX and ZZ bonds alternate in a two-qubit unit cell along the chain.

models.name: J-Q2 chain
models.description: Singlet-projector bonds and products of adjacent disjoint singlet projectors define a one-dimensional J-Q interaction.

models.name: Two-leg Heisenberg ladder
models.description: Antiferromagnetic exchange runs along two legs and across the rung in each two-qubit cell.

models.name: Square TFIM
models.description: Square-lattice nearest-neighbor ZZ bonds compete with a uniform transverse X field.

models.name: Triangular AF TFIM
models.description: Antiferromagnetic Ising bonds on triangles combine geometric frustration with transverse-field fluctuations.

models.name: Square J1-J2 Heisenberg
models.description: Nearest-neighbor exchange competes with both next-nearest diagonal exchanges on the square lattice.

models.name: Triangular AF Heisenberg
models.description: Nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic spin exchange acts on a triangular lattice.

models.name: Kagome AF Heisenberg
models.description: Nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange acts on corner-sharing triangles with three qubits per primitive cell.

models.name: Shastry-Sutherland
models.lattice: 2x2 square cell; species x+2y; diagonals on even-even and odd-odd plaquettes
models.description: Square-lattice exchange and orthogonal dimer bonds are fixed at a known dimer-product ground-state point.

models.name: Square J-Q
models.lattice: square; both opposite-edge products on every plaquette
models.description: Square-lattice singlet-projector interactions include both opposite-edge products on each plaquette.

models.name: Square compass
models.description: Horizontal XX and vertical ZZ bonds tie the interaction component to the square-lattice direction.

models.name: Xu-Moore quantum plaquette Ising
models.description: Four-qubit Z plaquette interactions compete with on-site transverse X fields.

models.name: Honeycomb Kitaev
models.lattice: honeycomb brick convention: z intra,x B[-1,0],y B[0,-1]
models.description: Three bond colors select XX, YY and ZZ interactions on a honeycomb lattice with two qubits per cell.

models.name: Honeycomb Heisenberg-Kitaev-Gamma
models.lattice: honeycomb same bond convention as ID22
models.description: Honeycomb bonds combine isotropic exchange, bond-selective components and symmetric off-diagonal exchange.

models.name: Yao-Kivelson decorated honeycomb
models.lattice: A/B triangles; species 3*s+alpha, alpha=x,y,z; missing-color internal edge; external inherits honeycomb color
models.description: Each honeycomb vertex is replaced by a triangle, producing bond-colored couplings in a six-qubit cell.

models.name: 2D toric code
models.lattice: square edges: species0 +x,1 +y starting at cell
models.description: X-type stars and Z-type plaquettes act on the edges of an infinite square lattice.

models.name: Wen plaquette
models.description: Commuting four-qubit XYXY operators act around square plaquettes.

models.name: Honeycomb color code
models.lattice: honeycomb ID22 graph; one hexagon per cell; vertex qubits
models.description: X- and Z-type hexagon operators act on honeycomb vertex qubits.

models.name: Square cluster
models.description: A central X operator is dressed by Z operators on its four square-lattice neighbors.

models.name: Levin-Gu triangular Ising SPT
models.lattice: six neighbors cyclic a1,a2,a2-a1,-a1,-a2,a1-a2; original Bp minus sign preserved
models.description: Spin flips acquire phases from neighboring Ising domain walls at a triangular-lattice symmetry-protected topological fixed point.

models.name: Union-Jack CCZ SPT
models.lattice: A square vertex at integer r; B face center r+(1/2,1/2); four triangles per square
models.description: Spin flips dressed by controlled-Z phases arise from a controlled-controlled-Z circuit on the Union-Jack lattice.

models.name: Transverse-field Baxter-Wu
models.lattice: triangular basis; both upward and downward triangles
models.description: Three-spin Ising interactions on both orientations of triangular plaquettes compete with a transverse field.

models.name: BFG easy-axis kagome
models.lattice: kagome ID17; every hexagon all 15 pair interactions; exact additive constant retained
models.description: Easy-axis interactions couple all pairs around kagome hexagons, together with weak transverse exchange.

models.name: Kagome Heisenberg plus scalar chirality
models.lattice: kagome ID17; oriented triangles A0 B0 C0 and A0 B[-1,0] C[0,-1] are both CCW
models.description: Heisenberg exchange is supplemented by oriented scalar-spin-chirality terms on kagome triangles.

models.name: Simple cubic TFIM
models.description: Three-dimensional simple-cubic Ising bonds compete with a uniform transverse field.

models.name: Simple cubic J1-J2 Heisenberg
models.lattice: simple cubic; NNN all face diagonals
models.description: Simple-cubic nearest-neighbor exchange competes with exchange across all face diagonals.

models.name: BCC J1-J2 Heisenberg
models.description: Competing exchange couplings connect nearest and next-nearest neighbors on the body-centered cubic lattice.

models.name: Cubic compass
models.description: XX, YY and ZZ interactions are assigned to the three simple-cubic lattice directions.

models.name: Cubic transverse-field plaquette Ising
models.description: Four-spin Ising interactions occupy all three plaquette orientations and compete with a transverse field.

models.name: Pyrochlore XXZ quantum spin ice
models.lattice: FCC a1=(0,1,1)/2,a2=(1,0,1)/2,a3=(1,1,0)/2; positions 0,a1/2,a2/2,a3/2; abstract qubit axes
models.description: XXZ exchange acts on corner-sharing pyrochlore tetrahedra in a four-qubit primitive cell.

models.name: Dimerized diamond Heisenberg
models.lattice: FCC primitive labels; A0-B0 strong, A0-B[-e_mu] weak
models.description: Strong intra-cell and weaker inter-cell spin exchange distinguish one diamond-lattice bond direction.

models.name: Hyperhoneycomb Kitaev
models.lattice: four-site primitive cell, explicit original-paper six-bond convention
models.description: Bond-selective XX, YY and ZZ interactions extend to the three-dimensional hyperhoneycomb lattice.

models.name: Hyperoctagon Kitaev
models.lattice: BCC primitive a1=(1,0,0),a2=(1,1,-1)/2,a3=(1,1,1)/2; explicit six bonds
models.description: A three-dimensional tricoordinated lattice carries bond-colored Kitaev interactions with four qubits per cell.

models.name: Hyperkagome AF Heisenberg
models.lattice: simple cubic primitive cell; exact positions from arXiv:2311.08210 Eq1, modulo cells; NN squared distance 1/8
models.description: Nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange acts on a three-dimensional corner-sharing-triangle lattice with twelve qubits per cell.

models.name: Cubic cluster
models.description: A central X operator is dressed by Z operators on its six simple-cubic neighbors.

models.name: 3D toric code
models.lattice: species mu is +mu edge starting at reference vertex
models.description: X-type vertex stars and Z-type face plaquettes act on cubic-lattice edge qubits.

models.name: X-cube
models.lattice: cubic edge species as ID45; X cube, Z planar crosses
models.description: Twelve-edge X cube operators and planar four-edge Z crosses define a cubic fracton Hamiltonian.

models.name: Checkerboard fracton
models.lattice: 2x2x2 cubic cell; species x+2y+4z; cubes lower-corner parity even
models.description: Eight-qubit X and Z cube operators act on one checkerboard sublattice of the cubic lattice.

models.name: Haah cubic code 1
models.lattice: F={0,ex,ey,ez},G={0,ex+ey,ey+ez,ez+ex}; Z uses reciprocal supports AND F/G swap
models.description: Two-qubit cubic cells support commuting X and Z interactions with the code-1 polynomial geometry.

models.name: Chamon
models.lattice: FCC even sites; primitive a1=ex+ey,a2=ey+ez,a3=ez+ex; odd center ex for reference stabilizer
models.description: Six-qubit mixed-Pauli stabilizers act on a face-centered cubic lattice.

models.name: Truncated-octahedral 3D color code
models.lattice: BCC Voronoi cells centered at Z^3 and Z^3+(1/2,1/2,1/2); qubits at Voronoi vertices; conventional cubic translations
models.description: Commuting X- and Z-type operators are defined on a truncated-octahedral cellulation with twelve qubits per translation cell.
